newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo's Nikkei average plunges to 13-month low.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo's Nikkei average plunges to 13-month low.

text.p: Tokyo stocks slid below the key psychological level of 19,000 Tuesday, shrugging off Monday's record close in the Dow Jones industrial average, to hit a 13-month low as investors were hounded by lingering worries over the Japanese economy.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 average plunged 549.81 points or 2.83 percent to close at 18,896.19. It was the lowest close since Dec. 5, 1995, when the index finished at 18,879.53.

The stock market shrugged off the effects of the Japanese yen's recovery against the dollar. It had previously been hurt by fears that the weak yen might spark foreign investors to sell their yen-denominated assets, dealers said.
The yen's rebound was sparked by a raft of comments from Japanese officials.
"An excessively weak or strong yen is not favourable for the Japanese economy," Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference Tuesday. "We want exchange rates to stabilise."
Mitsuzuka's comments echoed remarks by Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa on Monday that Japan would continue to act appropriately to deal with excessive movements in foreign exchange markets.
In early New York trading, the dollar fell to 115.40 Japanese yen from 115.72 yen in late dealings Monday.
But the slightly stronger yen, which normally helps the stock market because it boosts the dollar value of yen-based assets, could not snap the stock market out of its recent depression.
